reviews.title: Please remove the templates…
reviews.body:
I’ve been using c.ai+ for quite a long time and I pay for the subscription every month, so I really want to see the quality of the models improve.

There are several things I genuinely like about the new model. Its memory is noticeably better, and I really enjoy being able to experiment with different response lengths and styles, especially choosing between more narration and more dialogue depending on the scene.

However, there is one major problem that makes roleplaying with more complex characters increasingly frustrating: the model often ignores the character definition.

The character’s appearance is usually described well, and the general personality can be quite accurate. But when the definition contains specific behavioral rules or a more complicated emotional development, the model often does not follow them. For example, I can explicitly write that a character does not immediately acknowledge romantic feelings, may deny them, and may even distance themselves when they realize something is changing. Yet during an actual conversation, the character will often immediately become romantically interested and push the relationship forward.

This also seems to happen with many other bots, not just my own. Different characters can start feeling strangely similar because they follow the same familiar romance patterns and phrases instead of developing according to their individual definitions.

After using Character.AI for a long time, these repeated patterns have become very predictable. Phrases and scenarios such as “you’re playing with fire,” “no one else, just you and me,” or “no more lies, no more walls” appear so often that they can make otherwise interesting characters feel generic.

I would really like the model to pay more attention to the actual character definition and the specific relationship dynamics written there, rather than automatically following common roleplay tropes. A character who is supposed to hesitate, deny their feelings, create distance, or develop a relationship slowly should actually behave that way.

The improved memory and customization options are great steps forward. I just hope future models will put much more emphasis on following character definitions and maintaining individual personalities and relationship dynamics instead of falling back on the same familiar clichés.

reviews.title: Why character ai needs to listen to its community
reviews.body:
Character AI has a lot of potential, but lately, it can feel like the community’s feedback is not being taken seriously enough. The people who use the platform every day are the ones who notice its problems, suggest improvements, and know what makes the experience enjoyable. When thousands of users bring up the same concerns, those opinions should not simply be ignored.

One of the biggest things Character AI needs to improve is communication with its community. Users want to feel like their feedback actually matters. Instead of making changes without clearly explaining them, the developers should listen to what users are saying and explain why certain decisions are being made. Even if every suggestion cannot be implemented, acknowledging the community would make a huge difference.

Character AI also needs to remember what made people enjoy the platform in the first place. The creativity, conversations, characters, and freedom to create different experiences are what attracted many users. If updates make the platform feel less enjoyable or more restrictive, people are naturally going to become frustrated.

The community is not asking for everything to be perfect. People are asking to be heard. Character AI has a huge community that clearly cares about the platform and wants it to succeed. Listening to that community could help make Character AI better for everyone.

Please listen to your users. Take their feedback seriously, communicate with them, and work with the community instead of ignoring it. Character AI has the potential to be much better, and the people using it every day should have a voice in its future.
